1

 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 12.02.2020.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 12.02.2020 at about 12.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a TVS Wego bearing No. KA.40.EC.8960 which was ridden by his friend and standing on the side of the road, at Chintamani - Shildgatta road, near Konapalli village,
Kasaba hobli, Chintamani taluk, Chikkaballapura district, at that time the driver of the I-10 Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068 driven the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle in which the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider and also to the another vehicle and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Government hospital,
Chintamani, wherein first aid treatment was given and later he was shifted to Sanjayaghandi hospital, MVJ hospital, Bengaluru, wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient.
Prior to the accident
, petitioner was aged about 42 years, doing coolie work and also agricultural work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner became permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.20,50,000/- with interest.
3. After service of summons, both the respondents have appeared before the court through their respective counsels and filed separate written statement.

The respondent No.1- owner has appeared through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the cause and manner of accident, injuries and disability sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident.
The compensation claimed by petitioner is excessive, exaggerated, arbitrary and exorbitant.
Further submitted that the offending Car was insured with the 2 nd respondent insurance company and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the claim petitioner against him.

The respondent No.2- insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy in respect of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068 vide policy No.
OG-19-1548- 1801-00000521 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and Prakash K.V vs Poomalai on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155565723/
2 conditions of the policy.

Further it has denied the involvement of the offending Car bearing No.
TN.58.AY.6068 in the alleged accident and contended that, there is a delay in filing the FIR.

Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident by contending that the alleged accident was due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle who has parked the vehicle in the wrong side and contributed towards the cause of accident.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of I-10 Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068 by its driver, in RTA took place on 12.02.2020 at about 12.30 p.m. on Chintamani - Shidlagatta road,
near Konapalli village, Kasa hobli, Chinta- mani taluk, Chikkaballapura district ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14.
Further examined the MRO of Sanjayagandhi hospital as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P15 & P16.

Also the MRD of MVJ Medical College and Dr. Nagaraj B N,
Orthopaedic surgeon at SOADS hospital were examined as PW.3 & PW.4 and got marked the documents at Ex.P17 to Ex.P21.
6.
Heard the arguments and perused evidence that are available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.
In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 6.

Prakash K.V vs Poomalai on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155565723/
3 9.

On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Krishnappa who is the rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA.40.EX.8960 in which the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068.
In continuation the IO conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P3.
On perusal of Ex.P3, the accident spot is in the northern side of the road and from northern edge the accident spot is 5 feet away.
This shows that the driver of the offending vehicle by driving this vehicle in negligent manner dashed the petitioner in the footpath.

10. The Ex.P4 is the IMV report wherein the motor cycle of the petitioner bearing No.
KA.40.EX.8960 has got damages in its left side attachment wheel and the offending Car bearing No.
TN.58.AY.6068
has got damages in its front and left side of the body and also the another TVS motor cycle bearing No. KA.05.JW.3439 has got damages in its right attachment wheel.
This shows that the driver of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068 was driven the said motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner, as such caused the accident without controlling the said vehicle.
As such the negligence of the driver of Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068 is established.
11. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by deposing the negligence of driver of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068 and produced documents in support of his case to prove the alleged negligence.

The PW.1 was cross-examined at length by denying the negligence of the driver of Car bearing No.
TN.58.AY.6068 but nothing has been elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.

Thus, it can be concluded that, the negligence is on the part of the driver of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068 who caused the accident by driving the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068 in a rash and negligent manner.
12. Ex.P6 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the driver of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068.
The IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner and also to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.
13. As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068.
14.
The respondent No.2 insurance company even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
No rebuttal evidence is placed by either of the respondents.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the driver of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.

At this juncture, I would like to quote the following judgment wherein it states that;
2009 ACJ 287 ( National Ins. Co. V/s.
Pushparama and others), wherein it is held that, Certified copy of the criminal court records such as FIR, recovery and mechanical inspection of the vehicle or documents are of sufficient proof to reach Prakash K.V vs Poomalai on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155565723/
4 the conclusion that the rider was negligent.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

By relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068.
15.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

17. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by his negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
18. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 12.02.2020 which is caused by the driver of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068 which is belongs to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
19.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 42 years.
As per Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P7 the year of birth of the petitioner is shown as 1975.
The accident was took place on 12.02.2020.
Hence as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 45 years.
The petitioner has produced discharge summaries marked at Ex.P8.

As per Ex.P8 the petitioner was admitted to Prakash K.V vs Poomalai on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155565723/
5

MVJ Medical College & Research hospital from 12.02.2020 to 20.02.2020, Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics from 26.02.2020 to 06.03.2020 and again at MVJ Medical College & Research hospital from 01.12.2022 to 28.12.2022 and has sustained Zygomatic arch fracture with right infra orbital fracture and maxillary sinus fracture, left ZMC fracture and organic delusional disorder with mesenteric adenitis also has also underwent ORIF.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: By considering the nature of injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.70,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bill as per Ex.P9 amounting to Rs.94,077/- which are supported by medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P10.
The medical bill is not seriously disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieve these bill.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding off the same i.e., Rs. 94,100/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was doing coolie work and also agricultural work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has produced has not produced any documents.
In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered in the year 2020 at Rs.14,500/- p.m.

As per the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P8 - the petitioner was admitted to MVJ Medical College & Research hospital and Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics totally for the period of 45 days.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total 4 months period including 45 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,500 X 4 months = Rs.58,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.
Nagaraj B N, Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS hospital as PW.4 and got marked the documents at Ex.P20 & 21.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner has sustained facial bone fractures and left hand base of the middle finger avulsion fracture.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered disability of 10% .
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
No other expert evidence is lead by the respondents to impeach the credibility of the evidence of PW.4 doctor.
In this case as per the evidence of PW.4 doctor who assessed the disability of the petitioner assessed permanent physical disability of 10%.
As per the say of the petitioner he was doing coolie work and also agricultural work.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 8% to the whole body.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '14'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.14,500/- X 12 X 14 X 8% = Rs.1,94,880/- which is the total loss of future income.

6 d) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P8 discharge summaries, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 45 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P5 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous as well as simple in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
e) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 45 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

By considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.45,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 45 days in the hospital.
f) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
The petitioner got injuries in the alleged accident.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.

a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 70,000/-
b) Towards Medical expenses Rs. 94,100/-

c) Loss of income during laid up Rs. 58,000/-
period d) Towards loss of disability Rs. 1,94,880/-
e) Towards food nourishment and Rs. 30,000/-
conveyance f) Towards attendant charges Rs. 45,000/-
g) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/-
Total Rs. 5,31,980/-
20.
Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Car bearing No. TN.58.AY.6068 and it was in force as on the date of accident.

No evidence is placed by the respondent Prakash K.V vs Poomalai on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155565723/
7 No.2 insurance company to eschew their liability.
No other grounds are made out by showing the contributory negligence of the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence the Respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the liability of respondent No.1- owner.
The petitioner is entitled for the interest @ 6% p.a.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
21.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,31,980/- (Rupees Five lakhs thirty one thousand nine hundred eighty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2- insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
